title: image.h: MAX_PIXELS missmatched with MAX_WIDTH * MAX_HEIGHT
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) UHD Graphics 770 (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.6078) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-14700 (28 threads)

### Issue description

Hello everyone!
I am not sure if this is a bug in the error messages, or if the Image.MAX_PIXELS value is unintentionally low, but here the situation:

The image.h file defines the following image size limitations:
``` cpp
	enum {
		MAX_WIDTH = (1 << 24), // Force a limit somehow.
		MAX_HEIGHT = (1 << 24), // Force a limit somehow.
		MAX_PIXELS = 268435456 // 16384 ^ 2
	};

```
But trying to load an image larger than the supported limits gives this error:
`Too many pixels for Image. Maximum is 16777216x16777216 = 268435456 pixels.`

These two maximum pixel values are obviously very different.
For better readability, here a comparison of the MAX_PIXELS value and the claimed value in the error message:

- 268_435_456 
- 281_474_976_710_656

The last commit where these values where changed is [da0457f
](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/da0457fa29e1ea63f89b1e1d73e72c4dc80a9966#diff-5b6bb2902a75f25639fd2e55d700a9fdc980f7ea5a11e926d219749e2e64a12e)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1dd3292-284c-4a7a-ad94-5af415cd0f0a)

While this could simply be an incorrect error message, I am not 100% sure that the MAX_PIXEL value is correct.
It would make sense to restrict the image to a size that most GPUs would support, ie. 16384 as mentioned in the MAX_PIXELS comment. 

But that is not actually the what the code checks for. image.cpp checks the width, height and size separately. So having an Image with the dimensions of 16777216 x 1 is perfectly acceptable. 
I'm not really sure what a differing MAX_PIXELS value would achieves, since it is only ever used in those checks anyway.

That leads me to believe that the MAX_PIXEL value might not be correct, and should be increased to 281_474_976_710_656.


I came across this bug, because I tried to load a very large image at runtime as a pure in-memory image. It's surprising that I don't even have to option to chop it up into chunks to be used as textures. 

I hope this is helpful, cheers!

### Steps to reproduce

Using `Image.load_from_file`, on any Image larger than 16384 x 16384 .

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Images I used under are under NDA, sorry. If needed I'll try to create some with an image editor.
